question: What is the main goal of dietary counselling when you're working with a patient?

options.A: Enforcing hospital cafeteria meal schedules on patients
options.B: Helping individuals make sustainable food choices for health
options.C: Strictly prescribing medications for nutritional deficiencies
options.D: Eliminating all carbohydrates from the patient daily intake

explanation: You're helping patients build lifelong healthy eating habits, not just quick fixes. Great job thinking about long-term wellness! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h1)

question: Why are nurses often the best members of the healthcare team to give dietary advice?

options.A: They spend the most direct time with patients and understand their daily routines
options.B: They control the hospital food supply chain and kitchen staff
options.C: They have legal authority to write formal diet prescription orders
options.D: They are the only healthcare workers trained in human biochemistry

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses spend the most time with patients, we really get to know their daily lives and routines, making our advice much more practical. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of biochemical data collected during a nutrition check?
explanation: You got it! Lab tests like serum albumin give us hard biochemical facts about protein levels inside the body. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h2)

question: If you want to find out what a patient has eaten over the past 24 hours, what assessment tool do you use?
explanation: That's right! Asking a patient to recall everything they ate in the last day is a simple, effective dietary history check. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h2)

question: Why should you and your patient set nutrition goals together instead of you just giving orders?

options.A: Patients are more likely to follow goals they helped create
options.B: Patients always know more about clinical nutrition than nurses
options.C: Hospital policies legally prohibit nurses from choosing diet plans
options.D: Collaborative goals eliminate the need for future follow-up visits

explanation: Exactly! When patients have a say in their plan, they feel a sense of ownership and are way more likely to stick with it. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h3)

question: Which of these is a realistic, patient-centered nutrition goal?

options.A: Walking for twenty minutes after lunch four days a week
options.B: Losing twenty kilograms by the end of this month
options.C: Eating a much healthier diet starting immediately
options.D: Eliminating all food cravings within forty-eight hours

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is specific, achievable, and easy to measure. Small, steady steps lead to big wins. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h3)

question: What is the main point of using motivational interviewing during nutrition counseling?

options.A: Testing the patient on their knowledge of food biochemistry
options.B: Allowing the nurse to firmly dictate strict rules for weight loss
options.C: Speeding up the clinical consultation to save hospital time
options.D: Helping patients resolve their ambivalence about changing eating habits

explanation: Spot on. Motivational interviewing helps patients work through their mixed feelings so they can find their own inner drive to change. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h4)

question: Which of these questions shows great communication during a diet check-in?

options.A: Are you aware that eating junk food causes heart disease?
options.B: What types of snacks do you usually eat in the evening?
options.C: Why have you not followed the low-fat diet I gave you?
options.D: Do you eat too much sugar every single day?

explanation: You got it! Open-ended questions make patients feel comfortable talking openly without feeling judged or cornered. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h4)

question: A patient says they cannot afford the expensive fresh vegetables you recommended. What is your best response?

options.A: Explore budget-friendly local produce or frozen vegetable alternatives
options.B: Advise them to spend less money on entertainment to buy groceries
options.C: Insist that fresh organic food is the only way to heal their body
options.D: Tell the patient to skip vegetables entirely and take a multivitamin

explanation: Well done! Nursing care has to fit the patient's pocket. Finding affordable local options keeps healthy eating realistic. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing one's diet?

options.A: Cultural food traditions that conflict with medical diets
options.B: Possessing a strong personal desire to cook healthy meals
options.C: Lack of knowledge regarding food preparation skills
options.D: Financial constraints and the high cost of healthy food

explanation: Exactly! Wanting to cook healthy meals helps you succeed—it's a motivator, not a roadblock. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h5)

question: Why do nurses use the 'teach-back' method after giving health instructions?

options.A: Testing the patient's memory span after a long hospital stay
options.B: Checking if the patient truly understands the dietary instructions
options.C: Giving the nurse a break from talking during the clinic visit
options.D: Fulfilling mandatory legal paperwork requirements for discharge

explanation: Spot on! Having the patient explain things back in their own words is the safest way to ensure they truly understand. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h6)

question: How does using the 'plate method' help patients manage their meals?

options.A: It provides a simple visual guide for portion control and food groups
options.B: It calculates the exact chemical calorie count of every single meal
options.C: It replaces the need for any further nursing follow-up or assessment
options.D: It legally restricts how much food restaurants can serve customers

explanation: You nailed it! The plate method is a fantastic, stress-free way to show portion sizes visually without needing a calculator. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h6)

question: What is the main reason for scheduling follow-up visits after dietary counselling?

options.A: Punishing patients who failed to follow their meal plan
options.B: Re-assessing baseline anthropometric data from scratch every week
options.C: Charging additional consultation fees for hospital revenue
options.D: Monitoring progress, reviewing food logs, and adjusting goals

explanation: Right! Follow-ups let us celebrate wins, talk through struggles, and tweak the plan so it keeps working for the patient. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h7)

question: A patient hasn't been able to hit their strict diet targets over the past month. What should you do?

options.A: Modify the unrealistic goal into smaller, more manageable steps
options.B: Discontinue all dietary counselling because the patient is non-compliant
options.C: Scold the patient for failing to follow professional medical advice
options.D: Increase the strictness of the meal plan to force compliance

explanation: Spot on! If a goal is too tough, we don't give up—we team up to break it down into smaller, easier steps. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h7)
